rules.title: Notice to determine estate at will (tenancy termination and nonpayment notice to quit)
rules.requirement: A tenancy at will can be ended by either side with written notice of three months, or the rent-payment interval or 30 days (whichever is longer) if rent is paid more often than every three months. For nonpayment, the landlord gives 14 days' written notice to quit. A tenant who has not had a similar notice in the prior 12 months can stop termination by paying all rent due within 10 days, and the notice must say so.
rules.quoted_span: In case of neglect or refusal to pay the rent due from a tenant at will, fourteen days' notice to quit, given in writing by the landlord to the tenant, shall be sufficient to determine the tenancy;
rules.effective_date_note: Document does not state an effective date.
rules.key_value: 3 months' notice (or rental interval/30 days if longer); 14 days' notice to quit for nonpayment; 10-day right to cure

unverifiable_exemptions: tenancy must be at will (not a fixed-term lease)

parsed.doc_summary: MA G.L. c. 186, § 12 sets notice requirements to end a tenancy at will, including 14-day notice to quit for nonpayment and a 10-day cure right. One just_cause_eviction record.
